title: TSINR: Capturing Temporal Continuity via Implicit Neural Representations for Time Series Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Time series anomaly detection aims to identify unusual patterns or deviations from expected system behavior.

gap.claim: Reconstruction-based methods may learn and reconstruct anomalous training points because anomaly labels are unavailable, making it difficult to capture normal patterns.

contributions.claim: TSINR uses implicit neural representation reconstruction for time series anomaly detection.
TSINR parameterizes time series as continuous functions with implicit neural representations and uses a transformer-based architecture to predict those representations.
The method introduces an INR continuous function for learning inter- and intra-channel information and uses a pre-trained large language model to amplify intense anomaly fluctuations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their INR continuous function for learning inter- and intra-channel information as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that TSINR achieves superior overall performance on univariate and multivariate time series anomaly detection benchmarks compared with other state-of-the-art reconstruction-based methods.
The authors report that TSINR captures temporal continuity and is more sensitive to discontinuous anomaly data.
The authors state that their code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper addresses time series anomaly detection.
Existing reconstruction-based methods can reconstruct anomalous training points and fail to capture normal patterns.
TSINR applies implicit neural representation reconstruction, using a transformer to predict continuous-function representations of time series.

Spectral bias prioritizes low-frequency signals, while the method's continuous function and language-model component address temporal continuity, channel information, and intense anomaly fluctuations.
The authors report superior benchmark performance across univariate and multivariate datasets and state that code is available.

source_observation.claim: Implicit neural representations prioritize low-frequency signals and can be less effective on high-frequency abnormal data.

interpretation.claim: A representation's inductive bias can improve sensitivity to discontinuities while creating a weakness for high-frequency anomalies.

application.claim: When applying continuous implicit representations to anomaly detection, evaluate separately on low-frequency and high-frequency anomaly patterns.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how performance varies across specific anomaly frequencies or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, or numerical performance results.
The abstract does not describe the training procedure, model configuration, or computational requirements.
The abstract does not provide details about the pre-trained language model or the proposed INR function.
